brief.question: What do local reconstruction metrics omit about downstream decisions and finite-event computation in frozen graph-to-spike classifiers?
brief.answer: Exact message improvement and matched local terminal decoding can fail to preserve decisions, prefixes, and whole-network activity under controlled interventions.
brief.audience: CVPR reviewers and researchers working on ANN-to-SNN conversion, spiking graph learning, and efficient visual inference.
brief.domain_bridge: Graph propagation converts local activation errors into class-margin changes; finite-event codes add temporal state, so downstream decisions and activity must be audited directly.

main: exact local terminal equality/decision and activity mismatch

terminology.decision_fidelity: teacher prediction agreement and teacher-class margin
terminology.whole_network_activity: total nonzero scalar events across the network
terminology.finite_event: a legal signed event sequence over a fixed active-tick prefix

qualification_placement.repeat_when: interpreting adverse-rate results or conditional frequency

section_jobs.Introduction: State the finite-event failure mode, the two missing quantities, and the bounded audit.
section_jobs.Methods: Define exact interventions, invariants, and selection rules.
section_jobs.Results: Report decision and activity consequences with their evidence scope.
section_jobs.Discussion: Interpret the two mismatches and delimit the evidence.
section_jobs.Conclusion: Answer the opening question without adding a claim.

facts.statement: Legal one-event changes that reduce first-tick graph-message MSE worsen the teacher-class margin in 332/811 MNIST and 296/928 CIFAR10 message-improving interventions; rates are conditional on the intervention distribution.
facts.measurement_scope: reported data split and teacher setting

facts.statement: Two legal two-tick codewords have identical local decoded tensors and equal local event counts but can change downstream predictions and whole-network activity; first-prefix profile and absolute amplitude are uncontrolled.
facts.measurement_scope: reported data split and teacher setting

facts.statement: Four or eight active ticks closely match teacher accuracy for the historical exposed-test adapters, with converted accuracy within the reported small deviations of 91.02/54.94/68.77 percent ANN baselines.
facts.measurement_scope: reported data split and teacher setting

facts.statement: The first node site closes 54.08 percent (MNIST) and 23.54 percent (CIFAR10) of the one-tick teacher-disagreement gap on exposed validation data.
facts.measurement_scope: reported data split and teacher setting

facts.statement: The evidence supports a diagnostic reporting checklist covering decisions at every required prefix, the intervention rule and eligible set, and whole-network activity.

The study audits frozen DCGS-derived graph adapters on superpixel graphs with exposed splits and one teacher in the hard/temporal tests; it does not establish converter-wide frequency or a new converter.
